Ana W: Heads-up — noticed multiple clients in eu-west saw SSE streams drop around 55s after start when burst quota kicked in. Console telemetry shows `resume_failed` + `kv_cache_miss` on resume attempts.
Sam R: Ugh. Is this the sticky-routing fallback we added last week? Might be a routing hop that loses session affinity.
Mike L: I saw a similar spike in logs ~10:30 UTC: proxy returned 502 while kube sidecar thought conn was healthy. Posting excerpt: ```proxy: upstream reset (code=EPIPE)
runtime: session_id=abc123 resume_token=xyz status=resume_failed```
Tanya P: Do we have any concrete repro steps? Are clients doing half-close vs full close? SSE should tolerate client reconnects.
Ana W: Repro (quick): 1) start long SSE stream with small keepalive (15s), 2) trigger burst traffic to exhaust tenant quota, 3) server applies soft-shed -> connection closed. Client reconnects but the resume flow fails because KV cache entry was evicted during soft-shed.
Sam R: That explains the `kv_cache_miss`. Should the server accept resume even if kv missing (i.e., fall back to resending initial context) or force client to full restart? There's also billing implications if we replay tokens.
Mike L: From runtime POV, resuming without KV is risky for correctness for chat+KV. We can implement a cheap guard: if kv cache missing within grace window (configurable, default 60s), allow resume but mark session as potentially stale and emit a metric `resume_kv_miss_grace`.
Tanya P: Agree on a metric. Also console UX: we need per-route resume success rate and a hot alert when resume_kv_miss rate > 0.1% for a tenant. Currently dashboards don't have resume-specific charts.
infra-bot: [incident-bot] New event: sse_resume_errors spike for tenant=acme-corp at 1953219850.
Sam R: We should also look at routing policy: when quota triggers, we sometimes route to a cheaper region for burst handling which doesn't share KV. That creates resume mismatches. Maybe we should pin resumes to the original model/shard for the grace window.
Ana W: Pinning seems safest but could hurt capacity elasticity. Idea: try sticky-routing for the 60s TTL after disconnect, otherwise allow cross-region fallback but force full restart (and surface clear UX to customer).
Mike L: Implementation plan: - add `resume_ttl` (default 60s) in session store - when route changes, check `kv_shard_id` match - if mismatch and age < resume_ttl, prefer original shard for resume - emit `resume_shard_mismatch` metric if we can't.
Tanya P: For console, add a small banner on the connection details panel: "Resume attempted but KV unavailable; full restart recommended" with link to docs. Also add chart: Resume success % (by tenant, 1h/24h).
Ana W: Also want to avoid duplicate billing: if a client retries quickly and we replay from earlier point we might double-charge tokens. Add server-side idempotency for resume replays and a per-session token-offset checkpoint so we don't charge twice.
Sam R: Good call. We'll need coordination with billing team; I'll open a quick RFC.
Mike L: Quick patch I can try: allow resume when kv missing only if client supplies `prefer_full_replay=false` header. Example: ```Prefer-Resume: true
Resume-Token: xyz``` Fallback path forces restart.
Tanya P: Might be easier UX to have server return a deterministic error code: `410 resume_unavailable` with `suggested_action=full_restart` so SDKs can auto-retry correctly.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: runtime/kv-cache-grace v0.3.1 -> canary (eu-west) by mike at 1953220005
Ana W: Thanks. Action items: Sam open RFC for billing idempotency, Mike push canary with resume_ttl and metrics, Tanya add console banner and charts, I'll run tenant repros and collect traces.
Sam R: I'll also add an alert in ops: `resume_kv_miss_rate > 0.05%` for now.
Mike L: Canary patched. Watchlist: resume_kv_miss, resume_shard_mismatch, resume_success_rate.
Ana W: If we still see `resume_failed` after canary, next step is to lock sticky routing for 60s for affected tenants.
Tanya P: Cool — will prototype banner copy and wire chart panels.
Ana W: Thanks all :thumbsup:
